families.label: No board needed
families.blurb: Pods or cones only. Start here today.

families.label: Board plus grid
families.blurb: Pass, then move. The hard stuff.

drills.name: Sole taps
drills.summary: Ball stays under you. Tap the called marker with the bottom of your foot.
coaching: Ball never leaves the middle. Feet go to the marker, ball stays home.
Head up. If they are staring at the ball they cannot see the call.
Small steps in, small steps out. No lunging.

drills.name: Dribble around the colour
drills.summary: Take the ball with you, go around the called marker, come back to the middle.
coaching: The ball goes round the marker too. Leaving it behind does not count.
Little touches on the way out, then push and go on the way back.
This is the single best drill on this list for ages 5 to 8.

drills.name: Shoulder check
drills.summary: Two markers behind you. Look before the ball arrives, then go to the called one.
coaching: A partner or parent serves the ball in by hand or foot.
The call comes while the ball is travelling. They must look over the shoulder.
Scanning is the least trained and most valuable habit in youth soccer.

drills.name: One foot
drills.summary: Red only. Same foot every time. Pure repetition.
coaching: Side of the foot, ankle locked, plant foot pointing at the board.
Run this on the weak foot twice as often as the strong one.
No decision here on purpose. Build the motion before you add choices.

drills.name: Both feet
drills.summary: Red is left, green is right, called at random. Now it is a decision.
coaching: Expect the weak foot to be slower. That gap is the whole point.
If they are guessing before the call comes, shorten the interval.
Body shape should stay square to the board between reps.

drills.name: Pass test
drills.summary: Timed test. Alternate feet on the call, close range, flat board.
coaching: Benchmark test. Run it the same way every time or the number means nothing.
Record it once a month, not every session.

drills.name: Control test
drills.summary: Angled board sends it up. Control first, then pass. Twice the work.
coaching: Tilt the board back so the ball returns in the air.
First touch out of the feet, second touch passes. Two touches, not one.
A dead first touch is worth more than a fast second one.

drills.name: Long pass test
drills.summary: Same as the pass test, from distance. Weight and accuracy.
coaching: Distance punishes a loose plant foot more than anything else.
If they cannot reach the board cleanly, move in. Do not let them lash at it.

drills.name: Four colours
drills.summary: Pass the board, then dribble around whichever colour is called.
coaching: The rep is complete when they get back and hit the board again.
Watch for the ball being abandoned at the marker. That is the common cheat.

drills.name: Fixed rotation
drills.summary: Same four colours, always in the same order. Anticipation, not reaction.
coaching: Because they know what is next, they can move before the call. That is the skill.
Good starting point for a young kid who freezes on the random version.

drills.name: Five second shuffle
drills.summary: The colour changes every five seconds whether you got there or not.
coaching: Brutal one. The target can change mid-run, so they must keep re-checking.
Closest thing on the list to a real defender moving while you are on the ball.

drills.name: Six colours
drills.summary: Six markers instead of four. More to hold in your head.
coaching: Needs six markers. Cones with coloured tape work fine.
Set them out in the same arrangement every session or the times drift.

drills.name: Numbers beat colours
drills.summary: Colours and numbers both show. If a number appears, the number wins.
coaching: Markers need a colour on one face and a number on the other.
The rule inversion is the load. Getting it wrong is normal at first.
Do not run this with under-eights. The rule is too abstract.

drills.name: Pass and move test
drills.summary: Timed grid test. Pass, dribble the called colour, return.
coaching: Benchmark. Fix the grid size for a whole season so the numbers compare.

drills.name: Control and move test
drills.summary: Angled board. Control it, then dribble the called colour.
coaching: Hardest of the standard tests. Aerial control plus a decision plus travel.

drills.name: Elite test
drills.summary: Everything at once. Colours, numbers, and numbers take priority.
coaching: The ceiling test. Do not bother until the pass and move test is comfortable.

drills.name: Two board switch
drills.summary: Two boards. Hit whichever one is called.
coaching: Each board scores its own hits, so this one is fully verified.

drills.name: Board rotation
drills.summary: Boards are called in a fixed order. Move early.
coaching: Predictable order means they can travel before the call. Rewards anticipation.

drills.name: Board and number
drills.summary: Boards plus markers plus numbers. The full ecosystem.
coaching: Only worth building once you have three boards and a bored teenager.
